purpose: Part of the next-39-titles-c candidate titles, group 2 of 4, live CSM research, nums 1021-1030.

contentFlagModel.mappingNote: This research preserves CSM's current visible category label and proposes the nearest app level. Production catalog edits should be made only by the follow-up importer/reviewer.

entries.title: A Series of Unfortunate Events

violence.summary: Peril, tension, and mostly off-screen violence with some graphic images, including an adult striking a child, assaults, murders, and an apparent suicide.

language.summary: Some very crude language is voiced by a baby character ("shmuck," "bite me").

romance.summary: A forced marriage plot targets a 14-year-old, predatory in intent though motivated by her inheritance rather than sexual content.

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface drinking, drug, or smoking content.

handoffNotes: The three Baudelaire children are orphaned when their parents die in a house fire at the film's opening, and they face ongoing mistreatment and peril from Count Olaf throughout; this grief and loss theme may need gentle prose context.

entries.title: Spy Kids 2: The Island of Lost Dreams

violence.summary: Peril and action-style violence occur throughout, but no one is actually hurt.

language.summary: Mild language includes one almost-four-letter word.

romance.summary: CSM does not surface a meaningful sex, romance, or nudity concern.

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface drinking, drug, or smoking content.

violence.summary: Nonstop cartoon action features giant robots, molten lava rocks, evil toy troops, explosions, light-saber-style attacks, and crashes that may frighten younger viewers.

language.summary: Minimal profanity is limited to mild name-calling such as "freak" and "wimp."

romance.summary: CSM does not surface a meaningful sex, romance, or nudity concern.

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface drinking, drug, or smoking content.

entries.title: Addams Family Values

violence.summary: Violence is played for macabre humor: many attempted killings (several involving an infant), electrocution, an explosion and fire set during a camp play, gunshots, knife throwing, an attempted beheading, and serial-killer trading cards.

language.summary: Language includes "damn," "God" as an exclamation, and rude phrases like "eat me."

romance.summary: A voluptuous villain has explicit sexual designs on Uncle Fester, with seduction and discussions of virginity; a magazine shows scantily clad women, and there are discussions of sex and a child's sex-education reference.

drinking.summary: Cigarette and cigar smoking and vodka and champagne drinking appear, including a cocktail mixed for a baby as a dark joke.

handoffNotes: Dark, comedic treatment of death and a serial-killer antagonist run throughout the film's macabre humor; the tone is played for laughs but may need prose context for sensitive viewers.

violence.summary: The only concerning moment is a father-son argument that reaches near-yelling levels; otherwise no violence is flagged.

language.summary: "Butt" represents the strongest language used in the film.

romance.summary: Mild flirting, lots of handholding, and one sweet kiss, along with a fair number of scenes with shirtless high school boys.

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface drinking, drug, or smoking content.

entries.title: The Chronicles of Narnia: Prince Caspian

violence.summary: Lots of swordfights and battles, some brutal, including stabbing, archery, and one prolonged close-up duel; multiple character deaths occur, though little gore is shown beyond the odd cut.

language.summary: Mild profanity includes occasional phrases like "shut up" and "idiot."

romance.summary: Some mild flirting and a single tender kiss at the end; no sexual content or nudity appears.

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface drinking, drug, or smoking content.

handoffNotes: Wartime character deaths, deceit, betrayal, and a scary appearance by the White Witch occur throughout; this may need prose context for sensitive younger viewers.

entries.title: The Chronicles of Narnia: The Voyage of the Dawn Treader

violence.summary: Fantasy battles with swords and arrows, a giant sea serpent, and scenes of people being sacrificed; characters appear dead but are actually in a deep sleep, and the White Witch appears only in a character's mind.

language.summary: British insults such as "sod," "what the blazes," "bleedin'," and "thick," plus occasional "crap," "shut up," and "idiot."

romance.summary: One brief scene shows a couple flirting and embracing; a star manifests as a beautiful woman who captivates two male characters, and a girl wishes she were as beautiful as her older sister.

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface drinking, drug, or smoking content.

handoffNotes: A girl watches her mother taken away on a boat, presumably never to be seen again (though this ultimately resolves positively), and the broader quest involves lords who were "dispatched" and never heard from again; this separation/loss theme may need gentle prose context.

violence.summary: Lots of toothsome, scary faces, zombies, and evil men in charge of teens on an island; lizard monsters and zombies chase the gang and possess characters' bodies.

language.summary: Mild profanity includes "beeatch," "booty," crude expressions, and a French pickup-line reference.

romance.summary: A body-swap scenario carries suggestive humor, characters wear short skirts and tight tops, Fred is portrayed as a womanizer, and there is a kiss scene between Fred and Daphne.

drinking.summary: Marijuana references appear through song choice and character behavior (including Shaggy's love interest named "Mary Jane" with suggestive dialogue), and Velma is shown drinking alcohol at a bar.

violence.summary: Comic peril that may be too intense for younger viewers: ghoulish-looking ghosts and monsters, car chases, a monster harpooning the Mystery Machine, and a bad guy hitting Fred in the groin with a dart.

romance.summary: Kissing occurs, and Velma changes her look with Daphne's help (including a skintight purple outfit) to impress her love interest.

drinking.summary: Shaggy smells marijuana in one scene, and there is beer drinking in a bar.

entries.title: How the Grinch Stole Christmas

violence.summary: Constant cartoonish action includes fires (one started by a flamethrower), explosions, falls, wild rides, and crashes with no serious injuries; the Grinch's menacing contortions and cackling put a child repeatedly in danger.

language.summary: Profanity includes "hell" and "bitchin'," plus a threat to "hunt them down and gut them like a fish"; crude humor includes the Grinch exposing himself.

romance.summary: A married couple shares an exaggerated kiss, the Grinch falls into a woman's cleavage and strips to reveal fur with a garter belt, mistletoe is placed over his buttocks, and a character is forced to kiss a dog's rear end.

drinking.summary: The Grinch drinks from a bottle marked "XXX" and subsequently acts intoxicated.

handoffNotes: The Grinch's backstory of childhood bullying and cruelty underlies his isolation and misanthropy; this may warrant light prose context though CSM does not detail an explicit death/loss scene.
